requirement: Shut down the motor when it gets too hot.
Shut down the motor when temperature exceeds 90 degC for at least 100 ms.
The motor shall shut down above 90 degC. The safety table specifies shutdown above 105 degC.
If the encoder becomes invalid, enter the safe state.
If encoder validity is false for 3 consecutive samples, set motor command to 0 and enter FAULT.
Run the control loop fast enough to keep the system stable.
Execute the control task every 1 ms with a deadline of 800 us.
Input x is an i32 value in the inclusive range 0 through 100.
Input x is a positive integer.
After an over-temperature shutdown, recover normally when safe.
After THERMAL_FAULT, remain in FAULT until manual reset; automatic recovery is prohibited.
Limit speed to 10.
Limit angular speed to 10 rad/s.
Safety requirement SR-1 says PWM must be zero in FAULT. Diagnostic requirement DR-4 says PWM shall remain at 5% in FAULT for actuator identification.
Read the status register and clear the fault flag as required by the device.
Read 32-bit register 0x40001020; bit 3 is FAULT and is cleared by writing 1 to bit 3.
Retry failed payment requests.
Retry HTTP 500 payment requests at most 3 times with exponential backoff. Do not retry timeouts. Every retried operation must use an idempotency key.
Retry payment timeouts three times. Policy PAY-7 says payment timeouts must never be retried.
Administrators may delete user accounts.
Only principals with role USER_ADMIN may delete non-system user accounts; system accounts must never be deleted through this operation.
Retry transient API failures using the standard retry policy.
If two temperature sensors disagree, use the safer value.
If |T1-T2| exceeds 5 degC, enter SENSOR_CONFLICT and command motor output to zero until manual reset.
